groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–2 题
groups.material: Good morning. In today's headlines, Scotland's transport minister has warned of potentially extreme weather conditions as heavy snow is forecast across the country later this week. Orange warnings are in force for many areas for Wednesday and Thursday. The transport minister advised people in parts of Scotland covered by the orange alert to avoid travel on Wednesday. This is what he said to us: "The orange warning may be raised to red in some areas. That is a warning for snow that has never been seen since the modern system came into place in Scotland." The orange warning has been extended until 6 p.m. on Thursday. Trains, planes and ferries are also likely to be affected, with a wind chill that could see parts of Britain feeling as cold as minus 15 degrees Celsius. The head of road policing said, "I would urge drivers to take extra care on the roads for their journeys. Drivers should make sure they're prepared for their journey with warm clothing, food and drink, sufficient fuel and a charged mobile phone. There could be significant traffic delays, so please start to plan your journey now and consider if you really need to travel when conditions are this poor."

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 3–4 题
groups.material:
Romania's wetlands are coming back to life thanks to help from local communities, the World Wildlife Fund, and funding from the European Union. Roughly 2,224 acres of the picturesque Danube Delta—home to 300 species of birds—have been filled with wildlife. The land has been connected to the network of lakes and streams in the area.
"A lot of birds have migrated to the area, and one doesn't need to travel long hours anymore or go to other lakes to watch the birds," says Ion Meuta, Deputy Mayor of Mahmudia.
The area around Mahmudia, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site, is the third-most bio-diverse in the world, after Australia's Great Barrier Reef and the Galapagos Islands. Groups used earth-moving equipment to restore the waterways. Government officials proposed to protect the area's endangered wild fish by issuing a fishing ban over the next decade.

groups.title: Section A · 第 3 篇 · 5–7 题
groups.material: Scott Dunn recently awoke from a medically-induced sleep he'd been in after a car accident. He was heartbroken after realizing he'd missed his high school graduation. So his classmates decided to give him another chance. It was just a month ago that East Juniata High School seniors met in the school's auditorium for graduation. And last week, they did it again. Scott's car accident was on May 22nd, just three days before the ceremony. "I remember waking up in the hospital and asking mom what date it was. She told me it was the 28th," he said. "I looked at her and said 'I missed my graduation.'" The school's principal Mr. Fausey called Scott's mom Karen and said that everybody wanted to do something special for him. Students wore their caps and gowns and sat in the front of the auditorium. Scott's parents, Karen and Scott Senior, sat front and center. After brief speeches, Scott's name was called, only Scott's name. He walked across the stage as the audience cheered. A graduation for one. "I'm speechless," Scott said. "I don't know how to even explain it. I'm speechless to know that so many people are behind me."

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 8–11 题
groups.material:
M: How do you like your new flexible working arrangement? Do you enjoy working from home?
W: Yes and no. I find isolation challenging at times. Apart from my mother, not too many people I know have time for phone chats during working hours. I tried the library, but found I wasn't really keen on working there.
M: No, neither would I. I find the library a bit too quiet. I'd lack inspiration or stimulation, which would be counterproductive to getting a lot of work done.
W: I find the same thing. So, lately I've been going out to cafes occasionally. I love the noise, the people, the busyness of the café, the sense of being out in the world.
M: Coffee shops seem to have effectively become office spaces for so many people in this digital age, though I'm not sure how cafe owners feel about it—having so many people who go to their places to work rather than drink and eat.
W: Yes, some people seem to spend a lot of time there and not order much. The most annoying ones for café owners must surely be those usually only two of them who occupy a table for six with their laptops and paperwork.
M: They should sit at a table for two, not the table for six. Some obviously stay so long. They need to plug the laptops into a power outlet. I nearly tripped over someone's computer electrical lead the other day in my local café.
W: It's a double-edged sword. No doubt about that for a café owner. While remote workers help to keep the cafe full in quiet times, they can take up the valuable table space in busy periods.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
W: I'm going to start looking for another job. I can't see myself getting an opportunity to progress at my company anytime in the near future. And I really think my skills and abilities deserve a higher salary.
M: You're not going to quit, are you?
W: I'm thinking I might as well. Then I can devote more time and energy to finding a better position at another company.
M: But you've been at your present company less than two years, haven't you? This will be the third time you've left a job in the last five years. If you do several jobs in a relatively short span of time, prospective employers might perceive that you lack loyalty. That could make them wary and reluctant to employ you.
W: Unfortunately, loyalty doesn't pay. Even if I get a promotion at my company, it's likely to be less sizable than if I were to get a job elsewhere. And even if I get a promotion, I'm not guaranteed to get a raise. I had that experience at another company I worked at.
M: They wanted you to take on more work and responsibility but for the same amount of money?
W: More or less, yes. The way I see it, through having different jobs, I've gathered a lot of experience in different jobs and in different industries.
M: But potential employers might worry that, that experience is not deep, or thorough enough.
W: Perhaps, but I feel pretty confident that I can sell myself. You know what they say, "Fortune favors the brave."

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material: There is a saying that goes something along the lines of "You must love yourself first before you can love someone else." Similarly, I personally believe that you must be comfortable and happy in your own company before you can truly be yourself in the company of others. There is a massive difference between being lonely and being alone. Loneliness is a horrible feeling. However, you don't have to actually be alone to feel that way. Many times, I've felt lonely when surrounded by a big group of people. In contrast, being alone can actually be a blessing, particularly when you've actively chosen it. In my experience, being bored and alone is dangerous and can easily lead to the feeling of loneliness. The trick is to be active. Get outside, stretch your legs, do something cultural, buy yourself something tasty to eat or something pretty to wear. You don't have to take anyone else into consideration and can do whatever you please. Spending time alone also allows you to more efficiently take care of problems. And then, when it's time to be social and meet up with your friends, you will be fully there, because you won't have too much other stuff floating around in your mind. Having been alone for a bit, you will also appreciate your friends' company more, and chances are, your time spent together will be more worthwhile.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material: When I turned 12, I worked summers at my father's small brick cleaning business. I remember the harsh acid smell of the cleaning solution and the scraping sound of stiff iron brushes against rough brick. It was tempting to hurry a job—just finish. But anybody who worked for Thomas Kahoon had to meet his standards, and that included me. If I messed up, he made me stay late until I got it right. My father wasn't being mean. He demanded the same of himself. Every brick he cleaned on a house stood out like a red jewel in a white setting. It was his signature. In 1970, when I was 20, I got married and moved out of my parents' modest place into a housing project. Drugs and gang violence were just beginning to plague the projects. Some of my friends went to jail. Some were killed. My wife Verllen was 18 and nobody gave our marriage a chance. But we believed in each other and our faith made us strong. When we married, I worked as a stock clerk at Southwest Super Foods. It was hard, tedious work. Each Friday night a truck came, with cases of food that had to be unloaded, priced, and placed on shelves. Most of the stock clerks tried to get Friday night off. But I was always ready to work. By Saturday morning, all the cans and jars in my aisle were replaced with the labels facing smartly out, like a line of soldiers on review. That was my signature. I took pride in the job nobody wanted.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material: Watching more than three hours of television a day doubles memory loss in older people, a new study of more than 3,000 adults suggests. Scientists at University College London used memory and fluency tests on the same group of people six years apart. They found that those who watched on average less than three hours' television a day showed a decline of around four to five percent, while those who tended to watch more than three hours a day declined by an average of eight to ten percent. The research team say they believe the "alert-but-passive" nature of television watching may be creating stress on the mind which contributes to memory decline. Older people who watch more television are also less likely to undertake activities known to preserve mental functioning such as reading, or interactive screen-based pursuits such as using the Internet or playing video games. The researchers say that television viewing may be a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease, but more research is needed to establish a link. While watching television may have educational benefits and relaxation benefits, the researchers advise that adults over the age of 50 should try and ensure that television viewing is balanced with other contrasting activities. If you're concerned that the amount of television you're watching could have a negative impact on your health, you should limit the amount of TV you watch each day and undertake some healthy hobbies.

questions.prompt: What were people in parts of Scotland advised to do?
options: Evacuate the area with the orange alert.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What were people in parts of Scotland advised to do? 

 【翻译】 苏格兰部分地区的人们被建议做什么? 
 A)  观看天气预报。 
 B)  撤离橙色警报区域。 
 C)  避免在周三出行。 
 D)  准备足够的食物和饮料。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Avoid travel on Wednesday. 
 【定位】 P1 The transport minister advised people in parts of Scotland covered by the orange alert to avoid travel on Wednesday. 
 交通大臣建议橙色预警覆盖区域内的苏格兰民众，周三不要出行。 

 【信号】 建议动词 advised 直接领出动作 。信号是建议动词本身——录音里 The transport minister advised people in parts of Scotland covered by the orange alert to avoid travel on Wednesday. 中 advised…to 后面跟的 avoid travel on Wednesday 就是被建议做的事，听到 advised 立刻锁定它后面的动词短语。 

 【替换】 advised people in parts of Scotland covered by the orange alert to avoid travel on Wednesday ↔ Avoid travel on Wednesday. 几乎原句裁剪，去掉对象状语 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音开头说 heavy snow is forecast across the country，出现了 forecast 一词，A Watch the weather forecast. 就靠"看天气预报"这个原词诱你选；但录音从没建议民众去看预报，是答非所问。  借用原文：heavy snow is forecast across the country 

 B) 原词陷阱 录音多次出现 Orange warnings are in force for many areas 和 orange alert，B Evacuate the area with the orange alert. 借"橙色预警/区域"这些原词制造熟悉感；但录音只让"avoid travel"（别出行），从没说"evacuate"（撤离），动作被偷换了。  借用原文：Orange warnings are in force for many areas 

 D) 张冠李戴 录音后半对司机说 Drivers should make sure they're prepared for their journey with warm clothing, food and drink，出现了 food and drink，D Prepare enough food and drink. 就盗这组词；但这条是对"司机"说的、且本题问的是"民众"被建议做什么，对象和位置都错了。  借用原文：Drivers should make sure they're prepared for their journey with warm clothing, food and drink

questions.prompt: What did the head of road policing urge drivers to do?
options: Pay more attention to the roads.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the head of road policing urge drivers to do? 

 【翻译】 道路警务负责人敦促驾驶员做什么? 
 A)  更加注意路况。 
 B)  待在更安全的地方。 
 C)  携带更多手机。 
 D)  乘火车回家。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Pay more attention to the roads. 
 【定位】 P1 The head of road policing said, "I would urge drivers to take extra care on the roads for their journeys." 
 道路警务负责人说："我要敦促司机们在出行途中格外注意路况。" 

 【信号】 催促动词 urge 紧领核心动作 。信号是 I would urge drivers to take extra care on the roads 里的 urge——题干用的就是 urge，录音原话也用 urge，词后接的 take extra care on the roads 就是答案落点，听到 urge 立刻锁其后。 

 【替换】 take extra care on the roads ↔ Pay more attention to the roads. 同义替换：take care=pay attention 

 【排除】 B) 过度推断 录音末句 consider if you really need to travel when conditions are this poor 让人联想"找更安全的地方"，B Stay at a safer place. 借这股"安全"语感诱选；但 urge 后真正的动作是"take care on the roads"（在路上当心），不是"待在更安全处"，是过度推断。  借用原文：consider if you really need to travel when conditions are this poor 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音对司机说 a charged mobile phone（带一部充好电的手机），C Bring more mobile phones. 盗 mobile phone 原词并把"一部充电的"偷改成"多带几部"；不仅数量错，这也不是 urge 那句的核心动作，是答非所问。  借用原文：a charged mobile phone 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音说 Trains, planes and ferries are also likely to be affected，出现了 trains，D Take a train home. 借"火车"原词诱选；但录音是讲"火车也会受影响"，根本没催司机坐火车回家，与 urge 那句无关。  借用原文：Trains, planes and ferries are also likely to be affected

questions.prompt: What is the news report mainly about?
options: There is only one ecosystem in Europe.
The wildlife in Romania isn't well protected.
There are 200 species of birds in Romania's wetlands.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the news report mainly about? 

 【翻译】 这则新闻报道主要讲的是什么? 
 A)  欧洲只有一个生态系统。 
 B)  罗马尼亚的湿地再次繁荣。 
 C)  罗马尼亚的野生动物没有得到很好的保护。 
 D)  罗马尼亚湿地有200种鸟类。 

 【答案】 B （主旨题） Romania's wetlands thrive again. 
 【定位】 P1 Romania's wetlands are coming back to life thanks to help from local communities, the World Wildlife Fund, and funding from the European Union. 
 在当地社区、世界自然基金会以及欧盟资金的帮助下，罗马尼亚的湿地正在重新焕发生机。 

 【信号】 开头点题句定主旨 。新闻的主旨通常落在第一句导语。Romania's wetlands are coming back to life 开门见山点出整条消息的核心——罗马尼亚湿地正在复苏；后文的鸟类迁入、水道修复、禁渔提议都是围绕这一核心展开的细节。主旨题就锁这句开头的总述句。 

 【替换】 coming back to life ↔ thrive again 复苏 = 再度繁荣 
 Romania's wetlands ↔ Romania's wetlands 主体同为罗马尼亚湿地 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音从没说欧洲"只有一个生态系统"，There is only one ecosystem in Europe. 是凭空捏造，且 "only one" 这种绝对说法与新闻在讲某地恢复的事实毫不相干。 
 C) 与原文相反 录音盗用了 wildlife 这个词，The wildlife in Romania isn't well protected. 借它说"野生动物没被保护好"，但全篇是说湿地恢复、动物回归、政府还提出禁渔保护，方向恰恰相反，是把好消息说反了。  借用原文：filled with wildlife 

 D) 原词陷阱 There are 200 species of birds in Romania's wetlands. 盗用了录音的 "species of birds" 制造熟悉感，但它只是篇中一个枝节数字，主旨题不能选细节项；何况录音明确说的是 home to 300 species of birds——300 种，不是 200 种，数字也被改错了。  借用原文：home to 300 species of birds

questions.prompt: What did government officials propose to do to protect the endangered fish?
options: Prohibit fishing in the next 10 years.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did government officials propose to do to protect the endangered fish? 

 【翻译】 政府官员提议采取什么措施来保护濒危鱼类? 
 A)  封锁水道。 
 B)  恢复捕鱼禁令。 
 C)  使用监测设备。 
 D)  在未来10年禁止捕鱼。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Prohibit fishing in the next 10 years. 
 【定位】 P3 Government officials proposed to protect the area's endangered wild fish by issuing a fishing ban over the next decade. 
 政府官员提议，通过在未来十年颁布禁渔令来保护该地区濒危的野生鱼类。 

 【信号】 提出做某事的动作句 。题干问"官员提出做什么"，定位就盯表"提出"的动词。Government officials proposed to protect…by issuing a fishing ban over the next decade 里的 "proposed…by issuing a fishing ban" 正是那个动作句，by 后面跟的"颁布禁渔令"就是具体做法，答案落在这里。 

 【替换】 issuing a fishing ban ↔ Prohibit fishing 禁渔令 = 禁止捕鱼 
 over the next decade ↔ in the next 10 years decade = 10 年 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 Block the waterways. 盗用了录音里的 "waterways"，但录音说的是用设备去 restore the waterways（修复水道），方向是修复、不是 block（阻断）；而且这是修复水道的动作，不是保护鱼的措施，把别处的动作安到本题上了。  借用原文：restore the waterways 

 B) 原词陷阱 Restore the fishing ban. 几乎照搬录音原词 fishing ban，极易"听到就选"；但录音是 issuing a fishing ban（新颁布一项禁渔令），不是 restore（恢复一项原有的禁渔令）——动词 issue 被偷换成 restore，意思变了。  借用原文：issuing a fishing ban 

 C) 答非所问 Use monitoring equipment. 盗用了录音里的 "equipment"，但录音说的是 Groups used earth-moving equipment to restore the waterways——是各团体用"挖土设备"修水道，既不是 monitoring（监测）设备，也不是官员保护鱼提出的措施，与本题问的事对不上。  借用原文：used earth-moving equipment to restore the waterways

questions.prompt: What happened to Scott a month ago?
options: He gave a performance in the auditorium.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What happened to Scott a month ago? 

 【翻译】 一个月前Scott发生了什么事？ 
 A)  他出了车祸。 
 B)  他参加了毕业典礼。 
 C)  他心脏病发作了。 
 D)  他在礼堂进行了表演。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） He had a car accident. 
 【定位】 P1 Scott Dunn recently awoke from a medically-induced sleep he'd been in after a car accident. 
 斯科特·邓恩最近从一次医学诱导的昏睡中醒来,此前他因一场车祸而陷入昏睡。 

 【信号】 开篇即点核心事件 。新闻开篇第一句就交代主人公遭遇,awoke from a medically-induced sleep he'd been in after a car accident 直接点出 car accident 这一核心事件,新闻"开门见山报事件"的特点使首句成为答案句。 

 【替换】 after a car accident ↔ He had a car accident. 几乎原句对应 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 He attended his graduation ceremony. 盗用了反复出现的原词 graduation;但题问 a month ago 时他出了车祸、恰恰"错过"了原定典礼(he'd missed his high school graduation),并未在一月前参加典礼,属答非所问。  借用原文：he'd missed his high school graduation 

 C) 未提及 He had a heart attack. 与正确事件"车祸"同属突发坏事、听感都急促,极易混;但原文只字未提心脏病,他遭遇的是 a car accident,此项把事件换成了原文没说的另一种。 
 D) 原词陷阱 He gave a performance in the auditorium. 盗用了原文真出现的地点词 auditorium;但原文 auditorium 是同学们聚集补办典礼的礼堂,从无他"表演"一说,属借原词无中生有。  借用原文：met in the school's auditorium for graduation

questions.prompt: What did Scott ask about when he regained consciousness?
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did Scott ask about when he regained consciousness? 

 【翻译】 Scott恢复意识后问了什么？ 
 A)  他发生了什么事。 
 B)  当时是几号。 
 C)  毕业典礼什么时候举行。 
 D)  他在哪里。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） What date it was. 
 【定位】 P1 "I remember waking up in the hospital and asking mom what date it was. She told me it was the 28th," he said. 
 "我记得在医院醒来,问妈妈那天是几号。她告诉我是28号,"他说。 

 【信号】 他亲口说出的问话 。答案句是他本人的直接引语 asking mom what date it was,动词 asking 后面紧跟的 what date it was 就是他问的内容,人物原话里"问了什么"即答案信号。 

 【替换】 asking mom what date it was ↔ What date it was. 问话内容原样对应 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 What happened to him. 像是承接"出了车祸"的合理联想,但题干问的是他苏醒后"问了什么",原文他问的是 what date it was,并没有问"自己发生了什么",此项答错了方向。 
 C) 原词陷阱 When the graduation ceremony was. 盗用了高频原词 graduation,又和正确项同样关乎"时间",极易混;但他问的是 date(几号),不是"典礼在何时",原文中典礼时间是后文交代、并非他苏醒时所问。  借用原文：met in the school's auditorium for graduation 

 D) 未提及 Where he was. 把疑问维度换成"地点";苏醒后问自己身处何地虽是常见桥段,但原文他问的是日期 what date it was,从未问 where,此项是原文没出现的内容。

questions.prompt: Why was Scott speechless at the graduation ceremony?
options: He was really touched by his classmates.
He didn't know what happened at all.
He couldn't remember what to say.
His parents wore caps and gowns.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why was Scott speechless at the graduation ceremony? 

 【翻译】 为什么Scott在毕业典礼上说不出话来？ 
 A)  他真的被同学们感动了。 
 B)  他完全不知道发生了什么。 
 C)  他记不起来该说什么。 
 D)  他的父母穿着学位袍和戴着学位帽。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） He was really touched by his classmates. 
 【定位】 P1 "I'm speechless," Scott said. "I don't know how to even explain it. I'm speechless to know that so many people are behind me." 
 "我说不出话来,"斯科特说。"我都不知道该怎么形容。得知有这么多人支持我,我激动得说不出话。" 

 【信号】 结尾本人道出缘由 。答案句在新闻收尾处,他自己点明 I'm speechless to know that so many people are behind me,speechless 后面的 to know that… 正是"说不出话"的原因——这么多人支持他,本人解释句即答案信号。 

 【替换】 so many people are behind me ↔ He was really touched by his classmates. 概括:被众人支持=被同学感动 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 He didn't know what happened at all. 借用了原文 I don't know how to even explain it 里的 don't know 字样;但他说的是"不知如何形容(激动)",并非"完全不知道发生了什么",事实上他很清楚同学为他补办了典礼,此项把意思扭反了。  借用原文：I don't know how to even explain it 

 C) 偷换概念 He couldn't remember what to say. 与 speechless/"说不出话"听感极近,最具迷惑性;但 speechless 在此是"激动得说不出话",原因是被支持感动,而非"想不起该说什么",二者并非一回事。 
 D) 原词陷阱 His parents wore caps and gowns. 盗用了原文确实念过的画面词 caps and gowns;但原文穿学位帽袍的是 Students(同学),不是他父母,且这画面与"他为何说不出话"无关,既张冠又答非所问。  借用原文：Students wore their caps and gowns and sat in the front of the auditorium

questions.prompt: What does the woman say is the disadvantage of working from home?
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say is the disadvantage of working from home? 

 【翻译】 女士说在家工作的缺点是什么? 
 A)  孩子们的干扰。 
 B)  安静的氛围。 
 C)  孤立感。 
 D)  更长的工作时间。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） A sense of isolation. 
 【定位】 P2 I find isolation challenging at times. Apart from my mother, not too many people I know have time for phone chats during working hours. 
 我有时觉得孤立很难熬。除了我妈妈，我认识的人里没几个在工作时间有空跟我闲聊。 

 【信号】 被问者直接应答 。男士先抛出 Do you enjoy working from home?，女士在回答里直说 I find isolation challenging at times.，这句被问者的直接应答就是答案信号。 

 【替换】 I find isolation challenging at times ↔ A sense of isolation. 同根词换说法 

 【排除】 A) 全文女士只提到 Apart from my mother，从未说孩子打扰，Her children's disruption. 是凭居家办公的常识脑补出来的，原文无据。 
 B) 原词陷阱 Quiet atmosphere. 盗用了原文 I find the library a bit too quiet. 里的 quiet，但那是男士评价图书馆，不是女士说的居家办公弊端，张冠李戴。  借用原文：I find the library a bit too quiet. 

 D) Longer working hours. 也是居家办公常被吐槽的点，但女士全程没提工时长短，属凭印象添加的未提及项。

questions.prompt: What does the man say is counterproductive to getting work done in the library?
options: It lacks the materials he needs.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say is counterproductive to getting work done in the library? 

 【翻译】 男士说在图书馆完成工作时什么是适得其反的? 
 A)  它不提供咖啡。 
 B)  它太安静了。 
 C)  它没有免费Wi-Fi。 
 D)  它缺少他需要的资料。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It's too quiet. 
 【定位】 P3 I find the library a bit too quiet. I'd lack inspiration or stimulation, which would be counterproductive to getting a lot of work done. 
 我觉得图书馆有点太安静了。我会缺少灵感或刺激，这会对完成大量工作起反作用。 

 【信号】 因果链指向起因 。男士说太安静会导致 lack inspiration or stimulation, which would be counterproductive，counterproductive 的源头顺着 which 往前推就是 too quiet，因果链就是答案信号。 

 【替换】 I find the library a bit too quiet ↔ It's too quiet. 近乎原句压缩 

 【排除】 A) It doesn't offer coffee. 借了后文咖啡馆话题里的 coffee 来诱选，但男士说图书馆的问题是太安静，从没说图书馆不供咖啡，答非所问。  借用原文：Coffee shops seem to have effectively become office spaces 

 C) It doesn't have free Wi-Fi. 原文从未提及 Wi-Fi，是利用办公缺网络这一常识硬造的未提及项。 
 D) It lacks the materials he needs. 把男士说的缺 inspiration or stimulation 灵感刺激，偷换成缺实体资料，概念被换了。  借用原文：I'd lack inspiration or stimulation

questions.prompt: What does the woman like about doing one's work in a café?
options: The sense of being out in the world.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman like about doing one's work in a café? 

 【翻译】 女士喜欢在咖啡馆工作的什么方面? 
 A)  置身于外面世界的感觉。 
 B)  它提供的咖啡。 
 C)  咖啡桌。 
 D)  舒适的工作条件。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） The sense of being out in the world. 
 【定位】 P4 I love the noise, the people, the busyness of the café, the sense of being out in the world. 
 我喜欢那种喧闹、人来人往、咖啡馆的忙碌，还有那种置身世界之中的感觉。 

 【信号】 I love 喜爱信号 。女士用 I love the noise, the people, the busyness 直接亮出喜爱信号，I love 后面一串并列就是她喜欢的点，是最明确的答案信号。 

 【替换】 the sense of being out in the world ↔ The sense of being out in the world. 原句直接命中 

 【排除】 B) The coffee it provides. 蹭的是咖啡馆 café 这个场景词，但女士 I love 的清单里是噪音、人群、忙碌，根本没提咖啡本身，答非所问。  借用原文：the busyness of the café 

 C) The coffee table. 利用 coffee 一词的近形干扰，原文从未出现 coffee table，是凭咖啡馆联想硬造的未提及项。 
 D) The comfortable working conditions. 把咖啡馆想象成舒适的办公环境，但女士喜欢的是热闹忙碌，原文未提舒适，属未提及。

questions.prompt: What is most annoying for café owners according to the woman?
options: People bring their laptops and paperwork.
People occupy valuable table space in quiet times.
People of two occupy a table for six.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is most annoying for café owners according to the woman? 

 【翻译】 根据女士的说法,对咖啡馆老板来说最令人恼火的是什么? 
 A)  人们什么都不点。 
 B)  人们带着笔记本电脑和文件。 
 C)  人们在清闲时段占据宝贵的桌位空间。 
 D)  两个人占用一张六人桌。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） People of two occupy a table for six. 
 【定位】 P6 The most annoying ones for café owners must surely be those usually only two of them who occupy a table for six with their laptops and paperwork. 
 对咖啡馆老板来说，最招人烦的肯定是那些通常只有两个人却占着一张六人桌、摆满笔记本电脑和文件的人。 

 【信号】 the most 最高级 。女士用 The most annoying ones for café owners must surely be 这个最高级加 surely 强调，直接把最招烦的圈定为后面那种人，最高级就是答案信号。 

 【替换】 only two of them who occupy a table for six ↔ People of two occupy a table for six. 原句改写为选项 

 【排除】 A) People don't order anything. 盗用了原文 not order much，但那只是女士先提的一般性烦恼，没被 the most 修饰，不点单不是最招烦的那条。  借用原文：spend a lot of time there and not order much 

 B) People bring their laptops and paperwork. 直接搬了原文 with their laptops and paperwork，但带电脑文件只是六人桌那种人的修饰细节，本身不是被点名最招烦的行为，原词陷阱。  借用原文：occupy a table for six with their laptops and paperwork 

 C) People occupy valuable table space in quiet times. 盗用了末段 take up the valuable table space，但原文说占用宝贵桌位是在 busy periods，并非 quiet times，时段被说反。  借用原文：they can take up the valuable table space in busy periods

questions.prompt: What makes the woman think about changing her job?
options: She is not satisfied with the salary.
She is not capable of the job.
She's received a job offer from another company.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What makes the woman think about changing her job? 

 【翻译】 是什么让这位女士考虑换工作? 
 A)  她对薪水不满意。 
 B)  她无法胜任这份工作。 
 C)  她经常加班。 
 D)  她收到了另一家公司的工作邀请。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） She is not satisfied with the salary. 
 【定位】 P1 And I really think my skills and abilities deserve a higher salary. 
 而且我真心觉得，凭我的技能和能力，理应拿到更高的薪水。 

 【信号】 I really think 主观加重语气标出真实理由 。她在 I really think my skills and abilities deserve a higher salary 里用 I really think 加重语气，亮出最直接的换工作动因——觉得自己值更高的薪水，这种当事人强调式的自述句就是原因题的答案句。 

 【替换】 my skills and abilities deserve a higher salary ↔ not satisfied with the salary "理应拿更高薪"="对现薪不满"的换说法 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 原文里她说 my skills and abilities deserve a higher salary，是在标榜自己能力强、配更高薪，选项却说她 not capable of the job，把意思反了过来。  借用原文：my skills and abilities deserve a higher salary 

 C) 未提及 对话从头到尾在谈薪水、晋升、忠诚，从没提到她"常加班"，She often works overtime. 是凭"职场"话题想当然补出来的，原文无据。 
 D) 与原文相反 她说的是 I'm going to start looking for another job——还没开始找，更没拿到 offer，选项 She's received a job offer from another company. 把"准备去找"夸成"已经拿到 offer"，与原文不符。  借用原文：I'm going to start looking for another job

questions.prompt: What does the man say about people who keep changing their jobs?
options: They may be considered as less loyal.
They won't get the promotion opportunities.
They should take more responsibility at work.
They will be given hiring priority.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about people who keep changing their jobs? 

 【翻译】 这位男士如何评价那些不断换工作的人? 
 A)  他们可能会被认为忠诚度较低。 
 B)  他们不会获得晋升机会。 
 C)  他们应该在工作中承担更多责任。 
 D)  他们将获得招聘优先权。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They may be considered as less loyal. 
 【定位】 P4 If you do several jobs in a relatively short span of time, prospective employers might perceive that you lack loyalty. 
 如果你在相对短的时间里做了好几份工作，未来的雇主可能会觉得你缺乏忠诚度。 

 【信号】 被问方男方的直接论断句 。题目问"男方怎么说"，答案就落在男方那段 prospective employers might perceive that you lack loyalty——这是男方针对频繁换工作者下的直接判断，正是该题答案句。 

 【替换】 might perceive that you lack loyalty ↔ considered as less loyal perceive…lack loyalty = considered as less loyal 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 男方只说雇主会觉得你不忠诚、因而 reluctant to employ you，谈的是"难被录用"，并没说"得不到晋升机会"，They won't get the promotion opportunities. 在男方这段里无据。 
 C) 张冠李戴 They wanted you to take on more work and responsibility 里的 more responsibility 确实被念到了，但那是男方在转述女方旧东家的做法，不是男方"对频繁换工作者"的说法，选项 They should take more responsibility at work. 盗了 responsibility 一词张冠李戴。  借用原文：They wanted you to take on more work and responsibility 

 D) 与原文相反 男方的判断是雇主会 wary and reluctant to employ you(迟疑、不愿录用)，方向是负面的；选项 They will be given hiring priority. 却说成"被优先录用"，把极性彻底反了。  借用原文：wary and reluctant to employ you

questions.prompt: What does the woman say would happen even if she got promoted in her current company?
options: She might have to do extra work every day.
She might not get a pay rise.
She might not get enough vacation.
She might not gain more experience.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say would happen even if she got promoted in her current company? 

 【翻译】 这位女士说即使她在目前公司获得晋升会发生什么? 
 A)  她可能每天都要做额外的工作。 
 B)  她可能得不到加薪。 
 C)  她可能得不到足够的假期。 
 D)  她可能无法获得更多经验。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） She might not get a pay rise. 
 【定位】 P5 And even if I get a promotion, I'm not guaranteed to get a raise. 
 而且就算我升了职，也不一定能涨薪。 

 【信号】 even if 让步句，转折后才是真意 。她在 even if I get a promotion, I'm not guaranteed to get a raise 用 even if 设让步——"升职"是铺垫，让步后的"不一定涨薪"才是她要表达的代价，正是答案句。 

 【替换】 not guaranteed to get a raise ↔ might not get a pay rise not guaranteed a raise = might not get a pay rise 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 take on more work and responsibility 里的 more work 确被念到，但那是男方追问女方"过去那家公司"的情形，不是"在现公司升职后"的后果；且选项 She might have to do extra work every day. 多出 every day，原文从未说"每天"，属夸大。  借用原文：They wanted you to take on more work and responsibility 

 C) 未提及 全程谈的是薪水、晋升、忠诚、经验，从没涉及 vacation，She might not get enough vacation. 在原文中毫无依据。 
 D) 与原文相反 经验在原文里是女方的正面收获 I've gathered a lot of experience，并非"升职后得不到"的坏处，选项 She might not gain more experience. 把它说成负面后果，方向相反。  借用原文：I've gathered a lot of experience in different jobs

questions.prompt: What benefit has the woman gained from changing her jobs frequently?
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What benefit has the woman gained from changing her jobs frequently? 

 【翻译】 这位女士从频繁换工作中获得了什么好处? 
 A)  经验。 
 B)  信心。 
 C)  财富。 
 D)  机会。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Experience. 
 【定位】 P7 The way I see it, through having different jobs, I've gathered a lot of experience in different jobs and in different industries. 
 在我看来，通过做不同的工作，我在不同岗位、不同行业里积累了很多经验。 

 【信号】 I've gathered + experience 的收获自述 。她用 I've gathered a lot of experience 这一"动词 gather + 名词 experience"的搭配，亲口说出频繁换工作的收获，正是 benefit 题的答案句。 

 【替换】 I've gathered a lot of experience ↔ Experience. gathered experience → Experience 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 I feel pretty confident that I can sell myself 里 confident 确被念到，但那是她描述自己的心态、回应别人对她经验不深的质疑，并不是"频繁换工作带来的好处"，选项 Confidence. 盗了 confident 一词答非所问。  借用原文：I feel pretty confident that I can sell myself 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音结尾的谚语 Fortune favors the brave 里有 Fortune，但那只是她引用的一句鼓励自己的俗话，绝非"换工作得到的好处"，选项 Fortune. 正是预读预警过的"谚语原词"陷阱。  借用原文：Fortune favors the brave 

 D) 原词陷阱 an opportunity to progress 里 opportunity 出现过，但那是她抱怨现公司"看不到晋升机会"，是她缺的东西、不是换工作的收获，选项 Opportunity. 盗用该词反着用。  借用原文：getting an opportunity to progress

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about being alone?
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about being alone? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于独处说了什么？ 
 A)  这是一种可怕的感觉。 
 B)  这可能是一件好事。 
 C)  这既无聊又危险。 
 D)  这是最舒适的状态。 

 【答案】 B （态度观点题） It can be a blessing. 
 【定位】 P1 In contrast, being alone can actually be a blessing, particularly when you've actively chosen it. 
 相比之下，独自一人其实可以是一件幸事，尤其是当你主动选择独处的时候。 

 【信号】 转折 In contrast 后才是真意 。前句 Loneliness is a horrible feeling. 讲的是『孤独』的坏，紧接着 In contrast, being alone can actually be a blessing 用 In contrast 转折，把话头转到『独自一人』并给出正面定性。转折信号之后那句才是对 being alone 的真正评价，正是答案句。 

 【替换】 being alone can actually be a blessing ↔ It can be a blessing. 近乎同句，只换主语措辞 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It's a horrible feeling. 抄了录音 Loneliness is a horrible feeling. 的原词 horrible feeling，但那句形容的是 loneliness（孤独），不是题目问的 being alone（独自一人）。听到 horrible feeling 就勾，正中原词陷阱。  借用原文：Loneliness is a horrible feeling. 

 C) 与原文相反 It's boring and dangerous. 借了录音 being bored and alone is dangerous 里的 dangerous，但原文说的是『又无聊又独处才危险』，是有条件的；并非给 being alone 本身定性为危险。把条件去掉直接说独处『就是』无聊危险，与原意不符。  借用原文：being bored and alone is dangerous and can easily lead to the feeling of loneliness 

 D) 过度推断 It's the most comfortable state. 用了 the most comfortable 这种最高级，把独处吹成『最舒适的状态』。录音只说它可以是 a blessing，从未说它是『最舒适』，属于无中生有的拔高。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say helps reduce one's feeling of loneliness?
options: To meet up with your friends.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say helps reduce one's feeling of loneliness? 

 【翻译】 说话者说什么有助于减少孤独感？ 
 A)  保持活跃。 
 B)  与朋友见面。 
 C)  出国旅行。 
 D)  向他人寻求建议。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） To be active. 
 【定位】 P1 The trick is to be active. 
 诀窍就是让自己动起来、保持活跃。 

 【信号】 建议句 The trick is to… 。前一句说『又无聊又独处会导致孤独感』，紧接着用 The trick is to be active. 给出对策。The trick is to 是典型的建议/方法信号，其后的 be active 就是说话人开出的药方，是答案句。 

 【替换】 The trick is to be active ↔ To be active. 原句核心动作直接对应 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 To meet up with your friends. 抄了录音 meet up with your friends，但原文说的是『独处一阵后再去见朋友，你会更投入』，讲的是见朋友的好时机，不是用来减轻孤独感的办法。听到 meet up with friends 就勾，正中原词陷阱。  借用原文：when it's time to be social and meet up with your friends, you will be fully there 

 C) 未提及 To travel abroad. 说出国旅行，录音只讲了 Get outside（出去走走）、do something cultural（做点文化活动），从未提到 travel abroad，属于无中生有。 
 D) 未提及 To seek advice from others. 说向别人求教，听起来合常识，但录音给的对策是 be active（自己动起来），全程没说要 seek advice from others，是凭常识硬填的干扰项。

questions.prompt: What is an advantage of spending one's time alone?
options: It provides a chance for people to think deeply.
It makes us treasure the time.
It enables one to identify true friends.
It helps us take care of problems more efficiently.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is an advantage of spending one's time alone? 

 【翻译】 独处的好处是什么？ 
 A)  它为人们提供了深入思考的机会。 
 B)  它使我们珍惜时间。 
 C)  它使人能够识别真正的朋友。 
 D)  它帮助我们更高效地处理问题。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It helps us take care of problems more efficiently. 
 【定位】 P1 Spending time alone also allows you to more efficiently take care of problems. 
 独处还能让你更高效地处理各种问题。 

 【信号】 列举好处的 also allows you to… 。录音用 Spending time alone also allows you to more efficiently take care of problems 直接陈述独处的一项好处，also 表明这是在罗列益处中的又一条，allows you to 引出具体好处，是答案句。 

 【替换】 more efficiently take care of problems ↔ It helps us take care of problems more efficiently. 几乎原词，仅调整语序 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 It provides a chance for people to think deeply. 说独处给人深入思考的机会，听起来合理，但录音列举的好处是『高效处理问题、社交时更投入、更珍惜朋友』，从没提 think deeply，属于未提及。 
 B) 偷换概念 It makes us treasure the time. 蹭了录音结尾 your time spent together will be more worthwhile 里的 time，但原文说的是『和朋友共处的时间更值得』，不是『珍惜时间（treasure the time）』。借 time 一词偷换概念。  借用原文：your time spent together will be more worthwhile 

 C) 偷换概念 It enables one to identify true friends. 蹭了录音 appreciate your friends' company more 里的 friends，但原文说的是独处后『更珍惜朋友的陪伴』，不是『辨别出真朋友（identify true friends）』。借 friends 一词偷换概念。  借用原文：you will also appreciate your friends' company more

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the speaker's father?
options: He is very demanding in his work.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the speaker's father? 

 【翻译】 关于说话者的父亲我们了解到什么? 
 A)  他是一个严厉的人。 
 B)  他对别人刻薄。 
 C)  他在工作中要求很高。 
 D)  他通常工作到很晚。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） He is very demanding in his work. 
 【定位】 P1 My father wasn't being mean. He demanded the same of himself. 
 我父亲并不是刻薄。他对自己也是同样的要求。 

 【信号】 否定澄清句定调 。My father wasn't being mean. 用 wasn't 主动否定'刻薄'这一负面解读，紧接着 He demanded the same of himself. 把父亲的真实形象定为'对工作和自己都要求高'——这种'先否定误解、再给真意'的句子就是答案信号。 

 【替换】 anybody who worked for Thomas Kahoon had to meet his standards ↔ very demanding in his work 高标准=要求高 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 He is a harsh person. 的 harsh 在录音里确实出现过，但那是 the harsh acid smell of the cleaning solution 形容清洁剂刺鼻的气味，根本不是说父亲这个人苛刻——典型听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：the harsh acid smell of the cleaning solution 

 B) 与原文相反 He is mean to others. 的 mean 录音里出现在 My father wasn't being mean.——是被 wasn't 否定掉的说法，选它等于把说话人否定的话当成了肯定的结论，方向正好相反。  借用原文：My father wasn't being mean. 

 D) 张冠李戴 He usually works very late. 里'待到很晚'对应 he made me stay late until I got it right，但那是父亲让'我'留下来重做，加班的是说话人自己，不是父亲；而且这是偶尔(做错时)而非 usually(通常)。  借用原文：he made me stay late until I got it right

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the housing project?
options: He was plagued by drugs and gang violence.
His parents would move into his new house.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about the housing project? 

 【翻译】 关于住房项目说话者说了什么? 
 A)  他搬出去并离婚了。 
 B)  他深受毒品和帮派暴力困扰。 
 C)  他在那里住了20年。 
 D)  他的父母会搬进他的新房子。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） He was plagued by drugs and gang violence. 
 【定位】 P1 I moved out of my parents' modest place into a housing project. Drugs and gang violence were just beginning to plague the projects. 
 我搬出父母简朴的住处，住进了一个公共住宅区。毒品和帮派暴力当时正开始侵扰这些住宅区。 

 【信号】 定位词后紧跟的描述句 。录音一出现定位词 a housing project，下一句立刻 Drugs and gang violence were just beginning to plague the projects. 给出对这个地方的直接描述——题目问的对象一出现，紧跟其后的那句往往就是答案句。 

 【替换】 Drugs and gang violence were just beginning to plague the projects ↔ He was plagued by drugs and gang violence 主语换了人但同义 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 He moved out and divorced. 前半'搬走'对应 I got married and moved out，但录音说的是结婚后搬出，全篇只字未提 divorced(离婚)；这一半凭空捏造，整项就错。  借用原文：I got married and moved out 

 C) 原词陷阱 He lived there for 20 years. 的 20 在录音里确实念到，但 when I was 20 说的是他结婚那年20岁，是年龄不是在那住了20年——数字被挪去说时长，对象偷换了。  借用原文：when I was 20 

 D) 与原文相反 His parents would move into his new house. 说父母搬进他的新家，而录音是'我'从父母处搬出 moved out of my parents' modest place，方向正相反，且录音从没提父母搬来。  借用原文：moved out of my parents' modest place

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the speaker as a stock clerk?
options: He was only responsible for unloading food.
He had to sign his name on every label.
It was a hard and tedious job.
He was required to work on Friday night.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the speaker as a stock clerk? 

 【翻译】 关于说话者作为仓库管理员我们了解到什么? 
 A)  他只负责卸载食品。 
 B)  他必须在每个标签上签名。 
 C)  这是一份艰苦而乏味的工作。 
 D)  他被要求在周五晚上工作。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It was a hard and tedious job. 
 【定位】 P1 When we married, I worked as a stock clerk at Southwest Super Foods. It was hard, tedious work. 
 我们结婚时，我在西南超级食品店做理货员。那是又苦又枯燥的活儿。 

 【信号】 直接的概括评价句 。录音点出身份 I worked as a stock clerk 后，紧跟一句 It was hard, tedious work. 对这份工作做整体定性——这种对工作'是个什么活儿'的直接概括句，正是问'当理货员是什么情况'的答案句。 

 【替换】 It was hard, tedious work ↔ It was a hard and tedious job work=job 近义替换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 He was only responsible for unloading food. 的 unload 对应 cases of food that had to be unloaded, priced, and placed on shelves，但录音说货物要卸货、定价、上架三件事都做，选项用 only 只留卸货，把职责框窄了，与原文不符。  借用原文：cases of food that had to be unloaded, priced, and placed on shelves 

 B) 偷换概念 He had to sign his name on every label. 的 label 对应 the labels facing smartly out，但录音是说他把罐头标签朝外摆齐、这是他的'招牌(signature 比喻)'，并非真在每个标签上签名；把 That was my signature. 的比喻签名当成了字面签名。  借用原文：the labels facing smartly out 

 D) 与原文相反 He was required to work on Friday night. 的 Friday night 录音里念过，但原文是别人都想请假、I was always ready to work 是他主动乐意上夜班，不是 required(被要求)；把自愿说成被强制，性质反了。  借用原文：I was always ready to work

questions.prompt: By what means did scientists at University College London measure memory loss?
options: By recording the time people spend on TV.
By using memory and fluency tests.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 By what means did scientists at University College London measure memory loss? 

 【翻译】 伦敦大学学院的科学家们通过什么方式测量记忆力衰退? 
 A)  通过记录人们看电视的时间。 
 B)  通过追踪人们的生活习惯。 
 C)  通过使用记忆力和流畅性测试。 
 D)  通过扫描人们的大脑。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） By using memory and fluency tests. 
 【定位】 P1 Scientists at University College London used memory and fluency tests on the same group of people six years apart. 
 伦敦大学学院的科学家们对同一组人，前后相隔六年，做了记忆力与流畅度测试。 

 【信号】 动作动词 used 紧跟方法 。答案句信号是表"使用某方法"的动作动词 used memory and fluency tests，问"用什么手段"的细节题，落点就在这个 used 后面带出的具体工具上。 

 【替换】 used memory and fluency tests ↔ By using memory and fluency tests. 原句动词转成 By doing 的近乎直译 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说 By recording the time people spend on TV.，借了录音反复出现的 television 话题词，但研究测量记忆用的是 memory and fluency tests，不是"记录看电视的时间"，这是听到 TV 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：Watching more than three hours of television a day 

 B) 未提及 B 说 By tracking people's living habits."追踪生活习惯"，录音通篇只提到用 memory and fluency tests，从未说追踪生活习惯，属于编造出来的手段。 
 D) 未提及 D 说 By scanning people's brains.，"扫脑"听上去很像测记忆的高科技方法，但录音明确用的是 memory and fluency tests，从头到尾没有提到 scan 或 brain scanning。

questions.prompt: What contributed to memory decline in the participants?
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What contributed to memory decline in the participants? 

 【翻译】 是什么导致了参与者的记忆力下降? 
 A)  连续数小时看电视。 
 B)  玩电子游戏。 
 C)  阅读书籍和杂志。 
 D)  上网浏览。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Watching television for hours. 
 【定位】 P1 Watching more than three hours of television a day doubles memory loss in older people, a new study of more than 3,000 adults suggests. 
 一项针对三千多名成年人的新研究表明，每天看电视超过三小时会使老年人的记忆力损失加倍。 

 【信号】 因果动词 doubles 连起活动与后果 。答案句的信号是 doubles memory loss 这个把"看电视"和"记忆损失"直接挂钩的因果动词，问"什么导致记忆衰退"，落点就在 doubles 前面的那个行为上。 

 【替换】 Watching more than three hours of television a day ↔ Watching television for hours. 具体时长概括为 for hours 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 B 说 Playing video games.，录音确实念了 playing video games，但那是作为"有助于保持脑力的活动"提的，方向是有益、不是导致衰退，听到原词就选会张冠李戴。  借用原文：interactive screen-based pursuits such as using the Internet or playing video games 

 C) 张冠李戴 C 说 Reading books and magazines.，录音里 reading 是与"保持脑功能"绑在一起的有益活动，不是导致记忆衰退的原因，借原词反向设套。  借用原文：activities known to preserve mental functioning such as reading 

 D) 张冠李戴 D 说 Surfing the Internet.，录音 using the Internet 同样是被列为"有益脑力"的活动，不是诱因，属典型的原词反用。  借用原文：interactive screen-based pursuits such as using the Internet

questions.prompt: What do the researchers say about their finding concerning the link between TV viewing and Alzheimer's disease?
options: Television viewing may be a potential factor for Alzheimer's disease.
Alzheimer's patients tend to watch television more than 3 hours a day.
Some research has confirmed the link between them.
Television watching is beneficial to Alzheimer's patients.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do the researchers say about their finding concerning the link between TV viewing and Alzheimer's disease? 

 【翻译】 研究人员如何评价他们关于看电视与阿尔茨海默病之间联系的发现? 
 A)  看电视可能是阿尔茨海默病的一个潜在因素。 
 B)  阿尔茨海默病患者往往每天看电视超过3小时。 
 C)  一些研究已经证实了它们之间的联系。 
 D)  看电视对阿尔茨海默病患者有益。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Television viewing may be a potential factor for Alzheimer's disease. 
 【定位】 P1 The researchers say that television viewing may be a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease, but more research is needed to establish a link. 
 研究者表示，看电视可能是老年痴呆症的一个风险因素，但还需要更多研究来确立这种关联。 

 【信号】 留余地词 may + 转折 but 限定结论 。答案句信号是 may be a risk factor 的不确定词 may，以及紧随的转折 but more research is needed，研究者用"可能、还需更多研究"把话说得留有余地，结论就落在这种谨慎表态上。 

 【替换】 may be a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease ↔ Television viewing may be a potential factor for Alzheimer's disease. risk factor 同义为 potential factor，may 原样保留 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 说 Alzheimer's patients tend to watch television more than 3 hours a day.，录音确有 more than three hours 这个数字，但那是讲"看电视时长与记忆损失"，从没说"老年痴呆患者每天看超三小时"，是借数字原词设的陷阱。  借用原文：those who tended to watch more than three hours a day 

 C) 与原文相反 C 说 Some research has confirmed the link between them.，但录音明说 more research is needed to establish a link——关联还没确立，C 用 confirmed 把"尚未证实"夸成"已证实"，程度严重越界。  借用原文：more research is needed to establish a link 

 D) 与原文相反 D 说 Television watching is beneficial to Alzheimer's patients.，录音里确有 educational benefits and relaxation benefits，但那是泛指看电视的一般好处，绝没说"对老年痴呆患者有益"，整体基调是看电视有害，D 完全反向。  借用原文：watching television may have educational benefits and relaxation benefits

questions.prompt: What do the researchers suggest older people do?
options: Watch television no more than 3 hours each day.
Balance television viewing with other contrasting activities.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do the researchers suggest older people do? 

 【翻译】 研究人员建议老年人做什么? 
 A)  每天看电视不超过3小时。 
 B)  在看电视与其他对比性活动之间保持平衡。 
 C)  观看一些教育类电视节目。 
 D)  进行更多体育锻炼。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Balance television viewing with other contrasting activities. 
 【定位】 P1 the researchers advise that adults over the age of 50 should try and ensure that television viewing is balanced with other contrasting activities. 
 研究者建议，五十岁以上的成年人应尽量确保看电视与其他相反类型的活动保持平衡。 

 【信号】 建议信号词 advise + should 。答案句信号是建议词 the researchers advise 加 should try and ensure，问"建议做什么"的题，落点就在 advise/should 后面带出的那个动作上。 

 【替换】 television viewing is balanced with other contrasting activities ↔ Balance television viewing with other contrasting activities. 被动陈述转成主动祈使，措辞几乎照搬 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说 Watch television no more than 3 hours each day.，录音里 more than three hours 确实念过，但那是描述研究发现的时长门槛，研究者给老年人的正式建议是"平衡活动"，并非"每天别超三小时"，借数字原词冒充建议。  借用原文：Watching more than three hours of television a day 

 C) 偷换概念 C 说 Watch some educational TV programs.，录音确有 educational benefits 一词，但那是说看电视"有教育益处"，研究者从没建议"去看教育类节目"，借 educational 原词偷换概念。  借用原文：watching television may have educational benefits 

 D) 未提及 D 说 Take more physical exercise.，录音结尾只笼统提到 undertake some healthy hobbies，从未具体建议"多做体育锻炼"，physical exercise 是凭健康常识脑补出来的。
